title: Add independent SYCL differential execution adapter
problem: SYCL implementations may select different devices, and asynchronous kernel errors need to be observed before stdout comparison.
example:
--route sycl uses icpx -fsycl; --route acpp uses AdaptiveCpp generic targets.
The launcher requests sycl::gpu_selector_v, records the device name/fp64 support,
and waits with wait_and_throw() before judging output.
design: Keep Intel SYCL and AdaptiveCpp compiler flags in one handwritten SYCL adapter. A mandatory GPU selector and explicit exception-aware wait prevent CPU fallback or pending errors from looking like a formatting pass.
tradeoffs: The caller supplies a working SYCL GPU runtime. Python tests check selection, launch/wait structure and flag overrides; accelerator execution is not qualified here.
docs: Use a GPU selector, launch one SYCL task, and retain its device name. Execution requires SYCL or AdaptiveCpp GPU support; a CPU fallback cannot pass.
